headline: This law ties federal student loan interest rates to the 10-year Treasury note rate, with caps, for loans first disbursed on or after July 1, 2013.
what_it_does: For new federal Direct Stafford loans, the interest rate equals the high-yield 10-year Treasury note rate plus 2.05 percentage points for undergraduates, capped at 8.25%. Graduate and professional students' unsubsidized Stafford loans get the Treasury rate plus 3.6 points, capped at 9.5%, and Direct PLUS loans get the Treasury rate plus 4.6 points, capped at 10.5%. Each rate is fixed for the life of the loan, and consolidation loans get the weighted average rate of the loans they combine, rounded up to the nearest one-eighth of a percent. The law also directs the Government Accountability Office to study the actual cost of federal student loan programs and report to Congress.

who_it_affects.group: Undergraduate students who borrow federal Direct Stafford loans
who_it_affects.how: Their interest rate on loans first disbursed on or after July 1, 2013 is set by the Treasury rate plus 2.05 points, with a maximum of 8.25%, and stays fixed for the loan's life.

who_it_affects.group: Graduate and professional students who borrow unsubsidized Stafford loans
who_it_affects.how: Their new loans carry a rate set by the Treasury rate plus 3.6 points, with a maximum of 9.5%, fixed for the loan's life.

who_it_affects.group: Parents and graduate students who borrow Direct PLUS loans
who_it_affects.how: New PLUS loans carry a rate set by the Treasury rate plus 4.6 points, with a maximum of 10.5%, fixed for the loan's life.

who_it_affects.group: Borrowers who consolidate federal student loans
who_it_affects.how: Applications received on or after July 1, 2013 get a new rate equal to the weighted average of the consolidated loans' rates, rounded up to the nearest one-eighth of a percent.

who_it_affects.group: Federal government budget scorekeepers and the Government Accountability Office
who_it_affects.how: The budget effects of the law are kept off specified PAYGO scorecards, and GAO must study the actual cost of federal student loan programs and report to Congress.

when_it_takes_effect: The rate provisions apply to loans first disbursed on or after July 1, 2013, and to consolidation applications received on or after that date.
